title: vendor-tile-voice-checklist-and-trial-provisioning-matrix
content:
Purpose:
This is a working brief to capture the final voice for vendor marketplace tiles + a pragmatic acceptance checklist and trial-provisioning matrix for partners. Goal is a single page we can hand to Partner Success, Marketplace Ops, and Legal for quick sanity checks before publishing.

Status notes / approach: (notes to self)
- Drafted after last partner-squad sync (2025-10-28).
- Priorities: clear value prop for engineers, security & billing assumptions visible, minimal copy length for tiles (mobile-first).
- Open questions flagged in TODOs below.

1) Tile voice guide (single-sentence + 1-line supporting blurb)
- Headline (7–9 words, engineer-facing): "High-throughput LLM inference — predictable latency, lower cost"
- Supporting blurb (20–30 words): "Deploy fast with Redwood’s managed inference: host or run privately with predictable SLAs, autoscaling pools, and integrated cost optimizations for production workloads."
- CTA (tile action): "Start free trial" or "Request dedicated capacity" depending on partner tier.
- Microcopy constraints: avoid product jargon (no "KV cache", "quantization"), prefer outcomes (latency, cost, SLA).

2) Required metadata and display fields (Marketplace ops checklist)
- Short name (<= 40 chars): Redwood Inference — Hosted API
- Long name (<= 120 chars): Redwood Inference: production-grade LLM inference for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments
- One-line tagline: "Predictable, cost-aware LLM inference for production apps"
- Logo: 512x512 PNG + transparent SVG provided in /assets/marketplace/logos/
- Category/tags: AI, Machine Learning, Inference, Developer Tools
- Privacy & data residency note: list supported regions and whether logs are retained by default
- Billing SKU mapping: list SKU ids (see JIRA-MKT-4123)
- Contact email for partners: partnerships@redwood.ai

3) Acceptance checklist (pre-publish) — must pass all fields before tile goes live
- Copy QA: headline <= 9 words; blurb <= 30 words; no proprietary customer names used
- Legal: approved TOS snippet linked, data residency statement approved by Legal (linked artifact CONFLUENCE-RTL-8421)
- Security: KMS/HSM integration disclosure present if partner requests private deployment
- Compliance: if tile targets EU/health verticals, attach EU Data Processing Agreement or vertical compliance note
- Technical: sample API snippet included (curl + SDK), plus 1 flow showing streaming response usage
- Telemetry: confirm marketplace telemetry ID wired to Redwood analytics (ops ticket ID recorded)
- Billing: free trial SKU configured, trial duration and usage caps documented
- QA: tile renders on mobile and desktop previews; deep link landing page reachable and not blocked by SSO

4) Trial provisioning matrix (decision table for Partner Success to provision trials quickly)
- Inputs (columns): partner-tier, requested-deployment, trial-duration, default-quota, requires-SLA-addendum, auto-approve-or-manual
- Rows (examples):
  * "indie-saas" | hosted | 14 days | 100k tokens | no | auto-approve
  * "midmarket" | dedicated (shared) | 30 days | 500k tokens | maybe | manual review by Sales Ops
  * "enterprise" | private (VPC/on-prem) | 45 days | 1M tokens | yes | manual + legal
- Notes: quotas expressed as token units; conversion table to estimated requests per minute in Confluence link.

5) Sample copy variations (A/B testing candidates)
- Variant A (focus on latency): "Bring predictably fast LLM inference to your app — sub-100ms p50 for common prompts."
- Variant B (focus on cost): "Slash per-token costs with smart batching and cache-aware serving — optimize inference spend."
- Variant C (focus on security): "Run inference in your VPC with KMS-backed keys and audit logs for regulated apps."
- Experiment plan: run each variant for 2 weeks on new signups; track CTR on "Start free trial" and trial->paid conversion.

6) Trial provisioning runbook (step-by-step for PS/ops)
- Step 1: Validate partner tier and intended workload (link to partner intake form).
- Step 2: Allocate trial SKU in billing system; set token cap per matrix above.
- Step 3: If private/dedicated requested, create tenant in staging, enable KMS config, and add to canary routing group.
- Step 4: Send partner tile preview link + acceptance checklist to partner; gather sign-off (email thread saved).
- Step 5: Monitor trial telemetry daily (latency, error rate, token consumption). Escalate to SRE if p95 latency or error budget exceeded twice in 24h.

7) Quick technical artifacts to include on landing page (minimal set)
- One sample curl request showing authentication and streaming
- One SDK quickstart (node/python) with 5 lines to get started
- Link to model catalog and recommended models for low-latency apps
- Link to pricing page and trial terms

8) Open questions / TODOs (for partner sync)
- Should enterprise trials require an NDA signed before provisioning? (legal opinion requested)
- Confirm the maximum token cap for midmarket (Finance input needed).
- Decide if we surface region availability per tile or only on landing page (UX input).
- Finalize CTA variants and experiment windows with Growth.

9) Risk & rollback plan (short)
- Risk triggers: sudden spike in token usage causing cost overrun; misconfigured public sample key; incorrect billing SKU mapping.
- Remediation: immediate disable trial SKU, remove tile from marketplace, and notify partner with remediation timeline.
- Backup: pre-approved fallback tile copy that removes trial CTA (low friction).

10) Owner notes / followups
- Samir: please add the exact billing SKU ids to linked_artifacts by 2026-01-05.
- Elena: coordinate with Legal to confirm DPA clause for EU health vertical; attach signed copy.
- PS: this doc should be copied into partner PR template once stable.

Appendix: quick QA testcases (for staging preview)
- TC1: Tile headline truncation test at 320px width -> no truncation; CTA visible
- TC2: Landing page SSL chain and HSTS enabled
- TC3: Trial token cap enforced at billing layer after 95% consumption alert
- TC4: KMS key rotation simulated and audited event present

End of draft.

-- Avery (notes: keep this doc minimal; split long legal/deep-ops content into linked Confluence pages and reference them. This is intended to be a concise handoff for Marketplace Ops.)
